spec.description: The power crossing Europe's borders every 15 minutes, as a graph Graphviz lays out in the browser (who powers whom, or where) beside the map and two Business Charts, cross-filtered by country and by step over the last two days.

options.content:
### Europe's power flows — who powers whom

The electricity crossing Europe's borders every 15 minutes, as a graph that **Graphviz lays out in your browser**: an arrow per border from the country that sends to the one that receives, as thick as the flow. *Who powers whom* ranks the senders on top and the receivers below; *Where* lays the same graph out from the map, over the last 48 hours. **Drag the slider, press play or click the chart below** to move every panel to another 15 minutes; **click a country** in the graph or the ranking to follow its borders everywhere.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT (SELECT count(DISTINCT reporter) FROM $flows)::BIGINT AS "Countries reporting",
       (SELECT max(time) FROM $edges) AS "Latest complete step"

spec.description: Countries reporting: how many of the eight countries asked answered on this load (Energy-Charts allows four requests at once; the rest come on the next refresh). Latest complete step: the newest 15 minutes every operator has reported, usually one to three hours ago.
spec.title: The data now

spec.rawSql:
-- Every border at every ready step.
SELECT time, a, b, gw FROM $edges

-- The step and the country picked: the graph redraws when either changes.
SELECT $step AS step, $country AS country

-- The countries, their names and where they are.
SELECT iso, name, lat, lng, hub FROM $countries

-- The net of each reporting country: its own total, positive is import.
SELECT time, reporter AS iso, gw AS net FROM $flows WHERE neighbour = 'sum'

spec.description: From the edges dataset: every border at every 15 min step every operator has reported, over the last 48 hours. A box per country, filled by what it sends (teal) or takes (amber) in all, an arrow per border carrying 50 MW or more, from sender to receiver, as thick as the flow. The eight reporting countries show their own net; for any other (dashed, with an asterisk) it is the sum over the borders it shares with them. Who powers whom: Graphviz dot, which ranks the graph so arrows point down. Where: Graphviz neato, started from the countries on the map. Click a country to pick it everywhere.
spec.title: Who powers whom — laid out by Graphviz in your browser

spec.rawSql:
-- The borders at the step picked on the graph, or the newest ready one,
-- from sender to receiver, in MW: what the flow layer draws.
WITH pick AS (
  SELECT coalesce(max(time) FILTER (WHERE time <= try_cast(nullif($step, '') AS TIMESTAMP)), max(time)) AS t
  FROM $edges
),
e AS (
  SELECT CASE WHEN gw > 0 THEN a ELSE b END AS src, CASE WHEN gw > 0 THEN b ELSE a END AS dst, abs(gw) AS gw
  FROM $edges JOIN pick ON time = pick.t
  WHERE abs(gw) >= 0.05
    AND ($country = '' OR $country IN (a, b))
)
SELECT o.lat AS lat0, o.lng AS lng0, d.lat AS lat1, d.lng AS lng1,
       round(e.gw * 1000)::BIGINT AS count,
       round(e.gw * 1000)::BIGINT AS mw,
       o.name || ' → ' || d.name AS border
FROM e
JOIN $countries o ON o.iso = e.src
JOIN $countries d ON d.iso = e.dst

-- The country picked, ringed. Empty until then.
SELECT name, lat AS latitude, lng AS longitude FROM $countries WHERE iso = $country

spec.description: The borders at the step picked on the graph or the chart (the newest complete one until then), each from the middle of the country that sends to the middle of the one that receives, in MW; only the borders of the country picked, when there is one (yellow ring). Circles add up what each country sends and takes over the borders shown.
spec.title: The same flows on the map

options.content:
**Source.** [Energy-Charts](https://www.energy-charts.info) by Fraunhofer ISE, its *cross-border physical flows* (`/v2/cbpf`), built on the ENTSO-E Transparency Platform: the power that physically crosses each border, in GW, every 15 minutes, over the last 48 hours every operator has reported. It is read on the server through the stack's gateway, which keeps each answer 10 minutes. Physical flows, not trade: power takes every path the grid offers, so it can cross a country on its way between two others.

**Which countries.** Energy-Charts reports one country's borders per request and allows two requests a minute, so this dashboard asks for eight whose borders, between them, reach most of the continent: Germany, France, Italy, Poland, Hungary, Sweden, Spain and Romania. Borders between two other countries (the Netherlands and Belgium, Austria and Czechia, Norway and Denmark…) are not seen, and the net of a country outside the eight (dashed, with an asterisk) only adds up the borders it shares with them.

**Which steps.** Operators report with a delay of one to three hours, and a step arrives with some borders at exactly zero until each operator does. Only steps every operator has reported are shown.

**The graph.** Built in your browser for each step and handed to [Graphviz](https://graphviz.org) compiled to WebAssembly ([Viz.js](https://github.com/mdaines/viz-js)). *Who powers whom* is the *dot* engine, made for hierarchies: it ranks the countries so arrows point down, and breaks a loop by turning one arrow up. *Where* is the *neato* engine, started from each country's position on the map.

<small>Data: Energy-Charts, Fraunhofer ISE, CC BY 4.0, from ENTSO-E.</small>

spec.rawSql:
-- Every step: the power crossing the borders seen.
SELECT time, sum(abs(gw)) AS gw FROM $edges GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

-- The borders of the country picked, into it (above zero) or out of it, per step.
-- Empty until a country is picked.
SELECT e.time, c.name AS neighbour, CASE WHEN e.a = $country THEN -e.gw ELSE e.gw END AS gw
FROM $edges e
JOIN $countries c ON c.iso = CASE WHEN e.a = $country THEN e.b ELSE e.a END
WHERE $country IN (e.a, e.b)
ORDER BY e.time

spec.description: From the edges dataset, every complete 15 min step of the last 48 hours. With no country picked: the power crossing every border seen, in GW. With one picked: its borders, what comes in above zero and what goes out below, the six that carry most in their own colour, and its net as a line. The dashed line is the step the graph, the map and the ranking show; click the chart to move them.
spec.title: Two days across the borders — click a moment

spec.rawSql:
-- Every country at the step picked: what it sends, in GW (negative: takes).
WITH pick AS (
  SELECT coalesce(max(time) FILTER (WHERE time <= try_cast(nullif($step, '') AS TIMESTAMP)), max(time)) AS t
  FROM $edges
),
e AS (SELECT a, b, gw FROM $edges JOIN pick ON time = pick.t WHERE abs(gw) >= 0.05),
side AS (SELECT a AS iso, gw AS sends FROM e UNION ALL SELECT b AS iso, -gw AS sends FROM e),
seen AS (SELECT iso, sum(sends) AS sends FROM side GROUP BY iso),
-- Its own total, for the eight that report it: positive there is import.
own AS (SELECT reporter AS iso, -gw AS sends FROM $flows JOIN pick ON time = pick.t WHERE neighbour = 'sum')
SELECT c.iso, c.name, coalesce(o.sends, s.sends) AS sends, o.iso IS NOT NULL AS own
FROM seen s
JOIN $countries c USING (iso)
LEFT JOIN own o USING (iso)
ORDER BY sends DESC

spec.description: At the step the graph shows: what each country sends (right) or takes (left) in all, in GW. The eight reporting countries show their own total; any other (paler, with an asterisk) only adds up the borders of 50 MW or more it shares with them, as in the graph. Click a bar to pick the country everywhere; click it again to let it go.
spec.title: Who sends, who takes — click a country

query.rawSql:
-- Server side: physical flows across the borders of eight countries, from
-- Energy-Charts (Fraunhofer ISE, on ENTSO-E data), from the day before
-- yesterday in Berlin on, 15 min steps, GW, positive = into the country that
-- reports it. Three calendar days, so that the last 48 hours are there even
-- just after midnight, when today has no complete step yet.
-- Energy-Charts sends no CORS headers and answers the Host header DuckDB
-- sends with 503, so DuckDB reads it through the gateway (10 min cache). It
-- reports one country at a time and allows two requests a minute, four at
-- once: eight countries whose borders, between them, reach most of the
-- continent. A country refused now (HTTP 429) is left out of this load and
-- asked again on the next refresh, five minutes on, when the limit allows.
WITH day AS (SELECT strftime((now() AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Berlin')::DATE - 2, '%Y-%m-%d') AS d0,
                    strftime((now() AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Berlin')::DATE, '%Y-%m-%d') AS d1),
hub AS (SELECT unnest(['de', 'fr', 'it', 'pl', 'hu', 'se', 'es', 'ro']) AS c),
res AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT c, http_get('http://feeds/energy-charts/v2/cbpf?country=' || c || '&start=' || d0 || '&end=' || d1) AS r
  FROM day, hub
),
doc AS (SELECT c, (r->>'body')::JSON AS doc FROM res WHERE (r->>'status') = '200'),
step AS (SELECT c, unnest(json_extract(doc, '$.data[*]')) AS s FROM doc),
v AS (SELECT c, (s->>'timestamp')::TIMESTAMPTZ AS time, unnest(json_keys(s->'values')) AS k, s->'values' AS vals FROM step)
SELECT upper(c) AS reporter, k AS neighbour, time, (vals->>k)::DOUBLE AS gw
FROM v
WHERE (vals->>k) IS NOT NULL

source.sql:
-- One row per border and 15 min step: the flow from a to b (a before b in
-- the alphabet; negative is from b to a), averaged over the sides that report
-- it. Only steps every operator has reported: the newest arrive with borders
-- at exactly zero until their operator does, and a step with more zeros than
-- a stray idle cable is not ready. The last 48 hours of those.
WITH per AS (
  SELECT time, count(DISTINCT reporter) AS reporters,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE neighbour <> 'sum') AS n,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE neighbour <> 'sum' AND gw = 0) AS zeros
  FROM $flows GROUP BY time
),
complete AS (
  SELECT time FROM per
  WHERE reporters = (SELECT max(reporters) FROM per) AND zeros <= greatest(2, 0.1 * n)
),
ready AS (
  SELECT time FROM complete WHERE time > (SELECT max(time) FROM complete) - INTERVAL 48 HOUR
),
e AS (
  SELECT f.time, f.reporter AS rep, c.iso AS nb, f.gw
  FROM $flows f JOIN $countries c ON c.id = f.neighbour
  WHERE f.time IN (SELECT time FROM ready)
)
SELECT time,
       least(rep, nb) AS a,
       greatest(rep, nb) AS b,
       -- gw is into the reporter: from a to b it is -gw when a reports, gw when b does.
       avg(CASE WHEN rep < nb THEN -gw ELSE gw END) AS gw,
       count(*) AS sides
FROM e
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY time, a, b
